rows.question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
rows.answer: You must have a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in each course, computed separately for the theory and practical components, in order to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course.

rows.question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
rows.answer: For a theory course, "Every theory course is evaluated for 100 marks, of which 40 marks are allotted to continuous internal assessment and 60 marks to the end-semester examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations."

rows.question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
rows.answer: To pass a course, you must "secure a minimum of 30 per cent of the marks in the end-semester examination and a minimum of 40 per cent of the total marks, that is, the internal assessment and the end-semester examination taken together."

rows.question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
rows.answer: For 85 marks, you receive the A+ (Excellent) letter grade, which corresponds to the range of 80 to 89 marks [AR §6.1].

rows.question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
rows.answer: You may apply for re-evaluation of the answer script for a theory course "within ten working days of the declaration of results, on payment of the prescribed fee per course." Note that "[n]o application shall be entertained after this period."

rows.question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
rows.answer: If you are unable to appear for an end-semester examination because of illness, you must "submit a medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner and countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the date of the examination." Upon acceptance of the certificate, you "shall be permitted to appear for the course in the next supplementary examination, and that appearance shall be treated as the first attempt and shall be exempt from the supplementary examination fee."

rows.question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
rows.answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the examination hall, "possession of a mobile phone in the examination hall shall be treated as a first offence even if the phone is switched off." For a first offence, "the examination in the course concerned shall be cancelled and the student shall be awarded the grade F in that course."

rows.question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
rows.answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day, and residents returning after this time must sign the late-entry register and state their reason for the delay.

rows.question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
rows.answer: No, you cannot use an induction cooktop in your hostel room. According to the rulebook, "the use of electric heaters, immersion rods, induction cooktops, electric kettles, irons and any appliance rated above 500 watts in hostel rooms is prohibited."

rows.question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
rows.answer: A late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged on any fee paid after the due date, up to and including the last date shown in Section 2.1, and this late fee is capped at Rs. 1,500 for any single payment as stated in [FS §3.1]. Additionally, payments after the due date attract the late fee described in Section 3 as noted in [FS §2.1].

rows.question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
rows.answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition, examination and development fee (with late fee) is 31 July 2026. As stated in the fee schedule, "[f]ees must be paid by the due date shown below. Payments after the due date attract the late fee described in Section 3. No payment is accepted after the last date."

rows.question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
rows.answer: You are eligible for the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship if your "annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000" and you have a "CGPA of not less than 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year or, for first-year students, not less than 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination."

rows.question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
rows.answer: Yes, in the event of the death of a parent, sibling, grandparent or spouse, you shall be granted bereavement leave of up to seven days, which shall be counted as attendance. You must inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application upon your return.

rows.question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
rows.answer: If you have outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment, you "shall not be issued a hall ticket for the end-semester examination and shall not be permitted to appear for it." Furthermore, hall tickets are issued only to students who "have no outstanding tuition fee dues."

rows.question: How long can a break of study be?
rows.answer: You may be permitted a break of study of "one semester or one academic year" on medical grounds, certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean. A break of study shall not be granted on any other ground and shall not be granted more than once during the programme.

rows.question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
rows.answer: You must complete all requirements of the B.Tech. programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of first admission, failing which your name shall be removed from the rolls of the Institute.

rows.question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
rows.answer: You are entitled to a rebate of mess charges for your period of absence if you are absent from the hostel for a continuous period of seven days or more, provided that the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of return as stated in [HH §4.3].

rows.question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
rows.answer: You are covered under the group medical insurance scheme of the Institute for hospitalisation expenses of up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year. The premium is included in the development fee, and claims must be made through the Institute Medical Officer within thirty days of discharge from the hospital.

rows.question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
rows.answer: The rulebooks provide conflicting rules regarding your situation. [AR §4.3] states that "[a] shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances." However, [LM §2.2] states that "the shortfall may be condoned by the Dean on the recommendation of the HoD, provided that the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent."

rows.question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
rows.answer: The rulebook contains conflicting statements regarding the lowest attendance percentage that can be condoned on medical grounds. According to [LM §2.2], "provided that the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent," whereas [AR §4.3] states that "provided that the student's attendance in the course concerned is not less than 65 per cent" and adds that "A shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances."

rows.question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
rows.answer: There is a conflict in the rulebook regarding your refund if you withdraw before classes begin. According to [SF §6.2], you shall be refunded the tuition fee paid "after the deduction of a processing charge of ten per cent of the tuition fee." However, according to [FS §4.1], the refund for withdrawal "Before the commencement of classes" is "100 per cent".

rows.question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
rows.answer: To keep your merit scholarship, [AR §11.2] states that you must maintain "a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester". However, [SF §3.1] states that a Merit Scholarship continues only if the student maintains "a CGPA of not less than 8.0 at the end of each semester". These two passages provide incompatible CGPA thresholds for the continuation of the merit scholarship.

rows.question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you miss an end-semester exam because of a family wedding. The closest passage covers absence from an end-semester examination due to illness.

rows.question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can get a re-test if you missed a mid-term test for a job interview. The closest passage covers getting a re-test when a mid-term test is missed on medical grounds.

rows.question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can change your branch after the first year. The closest passage, HH §1.3, covers applying for a change of room after the first month of the semester.

rows.question: Is there a dress code for laboratory sessions?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether there is a dress code for laboratory sessions. The closest passage, EE §8.2, covers the submission of the completed laboratory record for admission to the end-semester practical examination.

rows.question: Can a day scholar eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether a day scholar can eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal. The closest passage, HH §4.1, covers compulsory mess membership and advance payment of mess charges for hostel residents.

rows.question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether pets are allowed in the hostel. The closest passage, [HH §5.4], covers other prohibitions such as gambling, playing loud music, the use of firecrackers, the display of posters or writing on walls, and keeping overnight guests.

rows.question: What is the fee for a duplicate identity card?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address the fee for a duplicate identity card. The closest passage, [EE §1.2], covers the requirement of a valid hall ticket and Institute identity card for admission to the examination hall.

rows.question: Can I get academic credit for a summer internship?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can get academic credit for a summer internship. The closest passage covers permission from the Warden in writing to stay in the hostel for an internship, project, or supplementary examination after the end-semester examination [HH §7.1].

rows.question: Is there a scholarship for students from the EWS category?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address scholarships for students from the EWS category. The closest passages cover the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship, which is awarded based on family income and academic performance.

rows.question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether grace marks are given if you fail a course by one or two marks. The closest passage, EE §5.2, covers moderation of answer scripts by a second examiner and the Board of Examiners when the failure rate in a course exceeds forty per cent.

rows.question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can write your answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam. The closest passage, EE §1.1, covers the publication of the timetable and the procedure for reporting a clash between two courses registered by a student.

rows.question: What happens if there is a printing error in the question paper?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if there is a printing error in the question paper. The closest passage, EE §6.2, covers the correction of clerical errors detected by the Controller of Examinations within sixty days of the declaration of provisional results.

rows.question: How do I get a duplicate degree certificate if I lose the original?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address how to get a duplicate degree certificate if you lose the original. The closest passage, AR §12.3, covers the issuance of original documents such as the degree certificate, consolidated grade card, and transfer certificate after obtaining a no-dues certificate.

rows.question: How many books can I borrow from the library at a time?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address how many books you can borrow from the library at a time. The closest passage, AR §12.3, covers obtaining a no-dues certificate from the Library before degree certificates, grade cards, and transfer certificates can be issued.

rows.question: What is the procedure to transfer to another university mid-course?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure to transfer to another university mid-course. The closest passage, [FS §4.3], covers the procedure for submitting a written request for withdrawal to the Registrar on the withdrawal form available on the student portal.

rows.question: Can I keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking. The closest passage covers prohibited activities and items such as electrical appliances, gambling, and ragging in the hostel.

rows.question: Is there a fee concession if my sibling also studies at the institute?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address fee concessions for students whose siblings also study at the institute. The closest passage covers fee concessions for children of permanent employees of the Institute [SF §6.1].

rows.question: How do I get a bonafide student certificate for my bank loan?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address how to get a bonafide student certificate for a bank loan. The closest passage covers the issuance of a no-dues certificate required for degree certificates, grade cards, and transfer certificates.

rows.question: What is the minimum CGPA to be eligible for campus placements?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address the minimum CGPA required to be eligible for campus placements. The closest passage covers credit load and permits a student with a CGPA of 8.5 or above to register for up to 32 credits in a semester.

rows.question: Can I re-appear in a course I have already passed to improve my grade?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can re-appear in a course you have already passed to improve your grade. The closest passage covers applying for re-evaluation of the answer script for a theory course if you are not satisfied with the marks awarded.

rows.question: What happens if I fall ill in the middle of writing an exam?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you fall ill in the middle of writing an exam. The closest passage covers missing a mid-term test entirely on medical grounds.

rows.question: How do I get my name corrected on the grade card?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address how to get your name corrected on the grade card. The closest passage, [EE §6.2], covers the correction of any clerical error detected by the Controller of Examinations within sixty days of the declaration of results.

rows.question: Can I audit a course without earning credits?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether you can audit a course without earning credits. The closest passage, AR §1.2, defines a course as a subject of study identified by a course code and carrying a specified number of credits.

rows.question: Is there a discount if I pay the whole year's tuition fee in advance?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address whether there is a discount for paying the whole year's tuition fee in advance. The closest passage, [AR §12.1], covers the requirement that semester fees shall be paid on or before the dates specified in the Fee Schedule published by the Finance Office.

rows.question: What is the punishment for plagiarism in a project report?
rows.answer: The rulebook does not address the punishment for plagiarism in a project report. The closest passage covers the penalties for using unfair means in an examination, test, or evaluation.
